acceptance_evidence: CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.
completion_conditions: Shiki platform decisions are docs/adr/SADR-NNNN-<slug>.md and live platform citations resolve through SADR.
Target repositories keep docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md product decisions without ambiguity or forced renumbering.
Fresh installs and stamped upgrades preserve target ADR bytes and pass validation.
A legacy Shiki ADR is removed only when its install-stamp path and digest match, otherwise the upgrade stops before the first write.
Unit, shell, validation, fresh-install, and upgrade suites pass in CI on the exact PR head.

decisions: Use SADR for Shiki platform decisions and retain ADR for target product decisions. Collision-only refusal leaves targets unupgradable; per-target renumbering destroys stable platform identity.
Rename existing platform records to SADR-0001 through SADR-0018 and record the decision as SADR-0019. Update current citations, resolver code, fixtures, packaging, and operator guidance together.
Treat frozen .shiki evidence as history and do not mechanically rewrite completed Goal, Plan, Task, Ledger, Report, Handoff, or Runner prose.
Plan all legacy removals before any write. A present legacy path is deletable only when a readable existing stamp contains the path and its digest equals the current file digest.
Absent, unreadable, malformed, incomplete, or mismatching ownership evidence fails closed with all blockers and a byte-identical target tree.
After clean preflight, delete only proven legacy paths, copy SADRs, and refresh the stamp with SADR digests and no removed legacy path.
Keep namespace, resolver, shipped templates, and atomic cleanup in one vertical slice because no partial branch is independently safe and valid.
grill_with_docs.source: Architecture review and Requirements Definition for GitHub Goal #322 on 2026-08-07 after a real CubeShare upgrade produced ambiguous ADR references and a red full suite.

non_goals: Renumbering or rewriting target product ADRs.
Rewriting historical .shiki evidence that accurately records the former namespace.
Deleting a target-owned file without exact install-stamp ownership evidence.
Changing Guardian, Contract Approval, lock, CCA, or MergeGate semantics.
Repairing the separate installer defect that overwrites a target .gitignore during upgrade.
outcome: Shiki platform decisions use a collision-free SADR namespace, while target repositories keep their existing ADR namespace. Fresh installs and stamped upgrades remain deterministic, and an upgrade removes a legacy numeric Shiki ADR only when its recorded install-stamp digest proves that the file is still platform-owned and unchanged.
title: Separate Shiki platform decisions from target ADRs with a SADR namespace
